annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygons are discrete building/block footprints rather than a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion. The layer represents housing association property as identifiable real-world housing blocks/projects with attributes like corporation and counts, so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
Point features mark individual archaeological finds/cesspits at addresses, so this is a set of identifiable objects rather than measurements or events.
Point features marking selected archaeological locations/sites with object codes and captions. The layer is about identifiable archaeological objects/locations, not measurements or events.
Polygon features mark selected archaeological findspots, not a full-area tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is patch: bounded phenomenon areas representing archaeological sites.
Polygons mark selected park/plantsoen areas with barbecue rules, not a full tessellation or reporting units; this is a bounded zone/patch layer.
Polygons are discrete conservation-area boundaries, not a full tessellation; the main phenomenon is protected city/village heritage areas as identifiable bounded objects/zones.
Point locations mark survey/inventory observations of wild bees at places and years, so the decisive rule is event/occurrence over time rather than objects or measurements.
Point locations mark honey bee hives/colonies, and the main mapped phenomenon is the numeric amount of kasten/volken at each location, so this is a point amount layer.
Polygon zones map diffuse soil-quality classes across areas; this is a full-area thematic classification, so Geometry is PlainVectorRegion and Entity is CoverageDS.
Point layer of individual trees with species, planting year, and management attributes; each point is a distinct real-world object, not a measurement or event.
Point features represent individual trees as identifiable real-world objects; numeric fields like plant year and radius are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent individual trees as identifiable real-world objects; numeric fields like plant year and radius are just attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features are individual trees, a countable real-world asset/object. Numeric fields like Boomnummer, Plantjaar, and RADIUS are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point layer of local compost initiatives at specific street locations; the main phenomenon is identifiable real-world objects/facilities, not measurements or events.
Polygon areas named as camera zones/overlastgebieden; they are selected bounded areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units, so PlainVectorRegion + PatchDS.
Point features represent individual Canadian poplar trees with IDs, species, and management status; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features depict distinct crowd-monitoring sensor objects (cameras, WiFi sensors, 3D sensors); numeric fields are just object attributes, so this is PointDS + ObjectDS.
Polygon areas mark selected cultuurhistorische verkenningen and protected zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; best fit is patch areas.
Point features represent individual knotweed occurrences/patch locations with species and photo attributes; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Point features mark ecopassage barrier cases and planned/realized mitigation actions at locations; the decisive rule is that this is mainly about occurrences/interventions (event-like) rather than point objects or measurements.

Polygon/MultiPolygon features are discrete potential wind-energy areas, not a full tessellation, so PlainVectorRegion. The main mapped phenomenon is numeric capacity/expected yield for each area, so AmountDS rather than object or patch.
Point features mark individual stemlocaties/polling places, with vote totals as attributes; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or amount layer.

Point features mark reported/updated oak processionary caterpillar nests, and the layer is real-time with mutation dates and status changes (registered, removed, treated), so the decisive rule is event over object.

Polygon areas mark selected pedicab restriction/permission zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is patch: bounded zones with categorical access rules ('allowed', 'not allowed', standplaats restrictions).
Point geometry and the layer is about pedicab/coach standplaatsen (pitches), i.e. distinct real-world facilities/places; decisive rule: object.
Point features represent individual addresses/WOZ building objects with a mapped function category; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.

Polygons represent a near-complete partition by blokstraat units, so Geometry is VectorTessellation. The main phenomenon is a full-area categorical function mix classification (Wonen/Voorzieningen/Werken), so the entity is CoverageDS rather than AmountDS.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete administrative partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is VectorTessellation; they are reporting/statistical units with codes and area attributes, so entity is LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, and the layer is reporting-unit geography (buurten/wijken) with IDs and area attributes, so tessellation + lattice.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete area partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is VectorTessellation. They are reporting/statistical units (buurten) with codes and area attributes, so the entity is LatticeDS.
Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam; the layer is a reporting/administrative unit tessellation (buurten, stadsdelen) rather than objects or patches.
City districts are administrative reporting units that partition Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.
City districts are administrative reporting units that partition Amsterdam; this is a tessellation and the decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical unit -> LatticeDS.

The layer is a polygonal partition of Amsterdam into named areas/neighbourhood units, so it is a vector tessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting/statistical units with area attributes, which makes it LatticeDS rather than AmountDS.

Administrative area polygons (stadsdelen/wijken/gebieden/buurten) form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is a tessellation and the entity is reporting/statistical units (lattice), with area as an attribute rather than the main phenomenon.

This is a set of named Amsterdam practice areas / neighbourhood-like administrative regions that partition the city area, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is a reporting-unit lattice rather than an amount or object.

Polygonal practice areas form a near-complete area partition of Amsterdam, so geometry is VectorTessellation. They are reporting/administrative units with names, codes, and area attributes, so the entity is LatticeDS.
Polygons are selected noise-contour zones, not a full tessellation. The decisive rule is contour/interval-band representation for dB levels (50 dB areas and terrain boundaries).
Polygon bands represent noise contour classes (55-60, 60-65, etc.), so this is a contour/interval map rather than a tessellation or object layer.
Polygon regions represent noise contour bands (50-55, 55-60, etc.) from a noise map, so this is a contour/interval layer rather than a tessellation or object layer.
Polygon bands represent noise contour classes (dB ranges) rather than a full tessellation or reporting units; decisive rule is contour/isoline-style interval zones.
Point features are vote/stemlocatie locations, and the main mapped phenomenon is numeric election results (counts/percentages by polling station), so this is PointDS with AmountDS.
Point features represent identifiable green roofs at specific addresses; numeric fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon. Classified as object points rather than amount or event.

Land use polygons form an area-wide thematic classification (tessellation). The categories describe exhaustive land-use coverage rather than individual objects or reporting units, so CoverageDS fits best.
Point features mark distinct historical buildings/archaeological sites with names and functions, so this is an object layer; geometry is point-based.

The layer shows three bounded polygon shapes representing Amsterdam area boundaries used for comparison, not a full tessellation. The decisive rule is object/area footprint representation rather than numeric amount or coverage.
Polygon areas mark selected dog off-leash, ban, and restriction zones rather than a full tessellation or reporting units; the decisive rule is bounded phenomenon patches.

Polygon features are discrete named green areas/projects, not a full tessellation; the layer is about identifiable bounded green structure objects with area attributes, so ObjectDS fits better than coverage or amount.
Point features represent individual private elm trees (a countable real-world object); the numeric/categorical fields are tree attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features marking identifiable housing projects/buildings; numeric Aantal_woningen is an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon, so ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual chestnut trees as identifiable objects; the numeric field is just an attribute/ID, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point geometry with thousands of sampled locations and numeric groundwater/terrain variables (Maaiveld, GLG, GLG_maaiveld); the layer is a point-measurement map, not objects or areas.
Polygon regions show flood-risk/stress-test zones with probability and depth classes; they are selected bounded affected areas rather than a full tessellation or reporting units.
Point features mark fixed market locations; the layer is about identifiable markets (objects), not measurements or events.
Point features represent discrete identifiable green monuments/bijzondere bomen sites, not measurements or events. The decisive rule is points as real-world objects (ObjectDS).
Point features represent individual monumental trees, which are distinct real-world objects. Numeric and categorical attributes are descriptive, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point features represent identifiable monuments/buildings and related heritage objects; the main rule is object features at points, not amounts or events.

Point features mark actual occurrence locations of protected wall flora; the main map message is presence/occurrence at sites, not point measurements or amounts. Annual counts are attributes, but the layer is primarily an existence/occurrence map.

The layer represents NO2 measurements at monitoring locations, so the main phenomenon is sampled environmental measurement data. Geometry is point-based measuring stations/buisjes, and the decisive rule is PointMeasuresDS for point-sampled concentration values.
Point layer of NO2 measurement locations; the main phenomenon is sampled air-quality measurements at points, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.

Polygon regions form selected mapped zones of the Oergeul, an interpreted subsurface gulch area that does not appear to be a full tessellation or reporting unit; the decisive rule is bounded phenomenon patch.
Point observations representing bore/sounding measurements of subsurface geology; the map uses sampled point locations for measured values like Top_Pleistoceen, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.

Polygon layer of named development neighbourhoods; these are discrete bounded areas within Amsterdam. Geometry fits a tessellation, and the regions represent identifiable area objects rather than a numeric or full-area thematic field.
Point features represent discrete public toilet facilities/locations, not measurements or events; decisive rule is object at points.

Polygon features are neighbourhood/area units forming a near-complete area partition, but they represent selected policy zones with conditions for overnight stays rather than reporting units or objects; best fits tessellation + patch.
Polygons are discrete parking-standard zones that do not form a full tessellation; the layer represents selected bounded policy areas, so PatchDS.
Polygons represent named parks/green spaces as discrete bounded places, not a full tessellation; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for identifiable real-world bounded entities.
Postcode4 areas are polygon reporting units that form a near-complete partition of the city; the decisive rule is tessellation/reporting-unit classification, not the area attribute Opp_m2.
Polygon postcode areas form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, and they are reporting/statistical units with attributes like area and postcode, so this is a tessellation with lattice semantics.
Polygons represent postcode6 areas, which are reporting/statistical units that partition the city; classify as tessellation + lattice.
LineString infrastructure network of roads/transport priorities (plus- and main networks); decisive rule is connected route/system => NetworkDS.

Polygon areas represent priority network zones for pedestrian infrastructure, not a tessellated reporting layer. The decisive rule is network: the layer maps route/infrastructure system areas (plus- and hoofdnetten) rather than individual objects or amounts.
Point layer of named locations; each point marks a distinct real-world object/place (camera or sensor site with a privacy statement), so ObjectDS rather than AmountDS or EventDS.

Point features mark locations of privacy-related data processing cases, surveys, or pilots in public space; the decisive rule is point geometry with an event/occurrence-like meaning rather than objects or measurements.
Point features marking distinct car fleet scan/camera locations in public space; classified as identifiable objects rather than measurements or events.
Point features are voting locations/stemlocaties, and the main mapped phenomenon is vote totals and percentages shown by circle size. This fits point AmountDS rather than object or point-measurement.
Polygon layer shows selected drainage/problem areas from a Rainproof simulation; these are bounded phenomenon zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units, so PatchDS.

Polygon hydro units form a near-complete area partition, so geometry is VectorTessellation. The layer represents selected hydrological problem/solution zones from Rainproof rather than reporting units or a full-area classification, so PatchDS.

Polygons mark selected rainproof bottleneck areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is PatchDS for bounded phenomenon zones; geometry is PlainVectorRegion because the areas do not form a complete partition.
Polygons mark specific rainproof problem areas/locations from a 3Di simulation, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is bounded selected area/phenomenon patch.
Point layer of identifiable religious buildings/centers with names and addresses, so it is a point object dataset rather than a measurement or event layer.

The layer maps sidewalk segments along streets, so the decisive rule is a connected route/infrastructure system (network). The line features are street-side path segments with width attributes, not isolated objects or amounts.

Line features representing a route/roadway traffic regulation network (mopeds on the roadway); decisive rule is network over object because the lines describe connected street segments and directions, not isolated linear objects.
Point layer of identifiable public playground/sports facilities; numeric Oppervlak is just an attribute, so classify as object points.
Point locations of city farming sites; each feature is a distinct real-world place/facility, so ObjectDS fits. The decisive rule is point objects, not amounts or events.
Polygon features are discrete city-farming sites/parks with names and addresses, so they are real-world objects rather than a tessellation or coverage layer.
Point features mark where space seekers settled with the city pilot over the past 9 years; the decisive rule is event/occurrence at locations, not amounts or objects.
LineString street layer; the decisive rule is network infrastructure. 'Major streets' are connected transport routes, and the numeric field is just an identifier, not the main phenomenon.
LineString transport lines for district heating/cooling networks; decisive rule is connected infrastructure/network rather than object or amount.
Polygons are buffered representations of district heating/cooling network areas, and the decisive rule is network infrastructure rather than a reporting-unit tessellation or object layer.

Polygon areas mark selected housing development project zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is patch: discrete bounded planning areas with numeric housing counts as attributes, while the main phenomenon is strategic housing plan areas.
Point locations mark distinct local food/agriculture initiatives and businesses (named sites with addresses and categories), so this is a point object layer rather than a measurement or event layer.
LineString features representing Amsterdam tram and metro lines; the layer is explicitly a transport network, so Geometry is LineDS and Entity is NetworkDS.
LineString features depict the tram/metro network of routes and stops; decisive rule is network infrastructure, not numeric amount.

Point features represent tram stops/metro stations, but the layer’s main phenomenon is the connected tram-metro network and station system; point locations are network nodes, not generic objects or measurements.
Point features represent tram stops and metro stations, but the layer is primarily about the connected tram/metro system and lines rather than isolated objects; thus PointDS + NetworkDS.
Point features represent individual traffic-light-controlled intersections (distinct objects). The year/status fields are attributes of those objects, not a main amount layer.

Line network of roads is not the main focus; the layer maps traffic forecast volumes on road links. Line geometry with numeric traffic intensities as the primary phenomenon fits AmountDS, not ObjectDS or NetworkDS.
Point layer of voting locations (stemlocaties) with circle sizes representing vote totals/turnout; main phenomenon is numeric election amounts at points, so PointDS + AmountDS.

Point features represent individual trees to be replaced; BOOM_ID, species, planting year, and size classes are attributes of objects, not the main phenomenon. Classified as point objects, not amounts or events.
Point features represent distinct traffic information system objects/facilities (cameras, displays, polls, etc.) with IDs and attributes; this is a point object layer, not an amount or event layer.
Point features map distinct traffic information system installations (objects/facilities) with attributes; not a measurement or event layer.
Point locations mark discrete bird nesting/roosting places at addresses; the numeric year counts are attributes, not the main phenomenon. Classified as point objects rather than amount or event.
Point features represent individual benches in Vondelpark, with adoption/status as attributes. This is a discrete object layer, not a measurement or amount layer.

Line geometries represent street segments, and the layer’s main phenomenon is walkability/sidewalk width and crowding ratings along those lines. This fits a line-based amount/score thematic map rather than a network of routes.
Point features mark individual wall art works at specific addresses, so this is a discrete object layer rather than measurements or events.
Polygon areas form an area-wide classification of Amsterdam’s welstand levels, so this is a tessellation with coverage-style thematic zones.
Polygon layer of Amsterdam welstand areas forms an area-wide thematic classification by system/type, so it is a tessellation with coverage rather than objects or patches.
Point features mark WWII bombings, crashes, and shelling incidents at locations with dates; the decisive rule is event occurrence at points, not object or amount mapping.
Polygon project areas represent housing plans, and the main mapped phenomenon is numeric housing quantity (Totaal and related counts), not a full tessellation or reporting-unit layer.
Point features mark distinct self-build plot projects/locations in Amsterdam; despite numeric attributes, the layer is primarily about identifiable objects, not amounts.
Polygon layer of building-roof areas classified into thematic categories for solar-panel placement; this is a full-area categorical coverage rather than reporting units or selected patches.

Point features represent detected solar panel systems/locations, not measurements or events. Numeric fields are attributes (panel count and watt-peak) of the objects, so ObjectDS is the decisive entity rule.
Point features marking distinct named swimming and play-water locations; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
